output.summary: The turnover rise is real, not an HRIS artifact: counts match payroll and use the same definitions in both years. It far exceeds the peer rise (5 points against 19), so labor-market conditions alone do not explain it. Pay is cited at a steady share (58% to 61%), and nobody knows current market position. Schedule complaints rose sharply (19% to 48%). Monthly separations stepped up in March, when the Saturday policy took effect at all branches. They did not step up again at the ShiftWise go-live in April. Manager attribution cannot be tested because the manager field is stale. A 15% raise ($2.6M, irreversible) and manager penalties are premature or harmful. Pull branch-level separations, the ShiftWise comparison and a market benchmark first. A targeted pay adjustment can still be approved by 2027-01-05.
